facts.text: Sunset Village first saw settlers in the early 1820s after the 1821 Treaty of Indian Springs opened Creek lands to Georgia.
The community’s name, Sunset Village, dates to a modern development, though its exact origin remains undocumented.
Early settlers like the Mullins, Tysinger, Barron, and Cox families helped establish Baptist churches in the area during the 1850s and 1860s.
During the mid‑20th century, textile mills in Upson County drew workers, sparking new housing and infrastructure along State Road 74 in Sunset Village.
The area sits at about 752 feet above sea level, giving it a mild climate with average highs near 90°F in summer and lows around 35°F in winter.
Annual precipitation in Sunset Village averages roughly 50 inches, with thunderstorms peaking in summer months and occasional tornadoes matching the state average.
